subject: geography
title: Jurassic Coast Case Study

concepts.def: 95 mile World Heritage coastline in Dorset and East Devon.
Made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2001 for fossils and geology.
Chalk stacks at the eastern end formed by marine erosion.
Near-circular bay carved into folded limestone and clays.
Famous natural limestone arch west of Lulworth Cove.
Bring jobs but cause traffic, litter and path erosion. 🪨

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Jurassic Coast stretches ~95 miles.

It runs from Exmouth in East Devon to Studland Bay in Dorset.

Became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2001.

Lulworth Cove shows differential erosion.

Sea breached a hard Portland limestone band then scooped softer clay behind.

The harder chalk at the back stopped the bay growing further.

Tourism brings benefits and costs.

Roughly 14 million visits a year support jobs and shops.

But narrow lanes jam, paths erode and fossil hunting damages rare specimens.
